chunks: Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from 'Imran al-Halabi, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: A man was asked about a man who prays Friday prayer as four rak'ahs, does he recite aloud in them? He said, 'Yes, and the Qunut is in the second [rak'ah].'

key_terms.يَجْهَرُ: To recite aloud / to pronounce loudly

ai.seo_question: How many rak'ahs are in Friday prayer and when is the Qunut performed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the technical details of the Friday prayer, affirming that recitation is performed aloud (jahr) and specifying that the Qunut is raised in the second rak'ah. This ruling highlights the distinct jurisprudential position of the Ahl al-Bayt regarding the structure of Jumu'ah, distinguishing it from other prayers through these specific acts of devotion and audibility. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the ritual precision emphasized in Shia fiqh during the weekly congregational prayer.
